content: ASVIR inhibits the transporters OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1. Caspofungin, in minor cases, decreases tacrolimus levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Trofinetide, classified as a serious interaction, increases the levels or effects of caspofungin through other mechanisms. Trofinetide, an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may elevate plasma levels of substrates for these transporters. Co-administration with sensitive substrates should be avoided, and close monitoring is recommended. Caspofungin can increase valsartan levels or effects through other mechanisms, necessitating caution and close monitoring. Valsartan is a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1, as demonstrated in in vitro studies using human liver tissue. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to valsartan, requiring close monitoring. Voclosporin and caspofungin, when co-administered, may increase each other's toxicity through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Voclosporin, an OATP1B1 inhibitor, may increase the concentration of OATP1B1 substrates, necessitating monitoring for adverse reactions when co-administered with such substrates. The interaction between voclosporin and caspofungin is considered minor, with unclear clinical significance. Anaphylaxis has been reported during the administration of caspofungin (brand name Cancidas). Infusion-related complications, such as phlebitis (20-35%), fever (6-30%), diarrhea (6-27%), shivering (9-23%), rash (4-23%), increased serum alkaline phosphatase (9-22%), hypotension (3-20%), respiratory failure (2-20%), elevated transaminases (2-18%), septic shock (11-14%), pleural effusion (9%), and respiratory distress (up to 8%), have been observed. Other adverse effects include abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, anemia, decreased hemoglobin, neutropenia, chills, hypokalemia, dizziness, erythema, facial edema, flushing, hematuria, hyperbilirubinemia, increased serum creatinine, induration, myalgia, pain, paresthesia, pruritus, sepsis, tachycardia, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, pancreatitis, hepatic necrosis, liver failure, nephrotoxicity, and renal impairment. Blood and lymphatic system disorders include anemia, coagulopathy, febrile neutropenia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia. Cardiac disorders include arrhythmia, atrial fibrillation, bradycardia, cardiac arrest, myocardial infarction, and tachycardia. Gastrointestinal disorders include abdominal distension, upper abdominal pain, constipation, and dyspepsia. General disorders and administration site conditions include asthenia, fatigue, infusion site pain/pruritus/swelling, mucosal inflammation, and peripheral edema. Hepatobiliary disorders include hepatic failure, hepatomegaly, hepatotoxicity, hyperbilirubinemia, and jaundice. Infections and infestations include bacteremia, sepsis, and urinary tract infections. Metabolic and nutritional disorders include anorexia, decreased appetite, fluid overload, hypomagnesemia, hypercalcemia, hyperglycemia, and hypokalemia. Musculoskeletal, connective tissue, and bone disorders include arthralgia, back pain, and extremity pain. Nervous system disorders include convulsions, dizziness, somnolence, and tremor. Psychiatric disorders include anxiety, confusion, depression, and insomnia. Renal and urinary disorders include hematuria and renal failure. Respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders include dyspnea, epistaxis, hypoxia, and tachypnea. Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders include erythema, petechiae, skin lesions, skin exfoliation, urticaria, and toxic epidermal necrolysis. Vascular disorders include flushing, hypertension, and phlebitis. Hypersensitivity to the drug or its components has been reported. Dextrose diluents should not be used. Caspofungin should not be co-administered with cyclosporine unless the benefits outweigh the risks, as cyclosporine may increase the area under the curve (AUC) of caspofungin by approximately 35%. Anaphylaxis has been reported, necessitating discontinuation and appropriate treatment. Histamine-mediated adverse reactions, such as rash, facial swelling, angioedema, pruritus, warmth sensation, or bronchospasm, are possible. Cases of Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), some fatal, have been reported. Discontinue use at the first sign of hypersensitivity and administer appropriate treatment. In patients with serious underlying conditions receiving multiple concomitant medications, isolated cases of clinically significant hepatic dysfunction, hepatitis, and hepatic failure have been reported. A causal relationship has not been established. Patients with abnormal liver function tests during therapy should be monitored for worsening hepatic function, and the risk/benefit of continuing therapy should be evaluated. There is insufficient human data to determine whether there is a drug-associated risk for major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes in pregnant women. There are no data on the presence of the drug in human milk, its effects on breastfed children, or its impact on milk production. The drug has been detected in the milk of lactating, drug-treated rats. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother's clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child or maternal condition. Caspofungin is generally acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Reconstituted solutions should be stored at 25°C or less for up to 1 hour. Mix gently to obtain a clear solution and discard if particulate matter or discoloration is observed. Transfer 10 mL of the reconstituted solution to 250 mL of normal saline (NS), half-normal saline (1/2 NS), quarter-normal saline (1/4 NS), or lactated Ringer's (LR) solution. Use the infusion solution within 24 hours if stored at room temperature or within 48 hours if refrigerated at 2-8°C. If 70 mg vials are unavailable for preparing the loading dose, reconstitute two 50 mg vials and transfer 14 mL to 250 mL of NS, 1/2 NS, 1/4 NS, or LR. For a 35 mg dose, reconstitute a 50 mg vial with 10 mL and transfer 7 mL to 250 mL (or 100 mL if medically necessary) infusion solution. Administer the infusion intravenously over 1 hour. Store vials at 2-8°C (36-46°F). Caspofungin is used to treat various fungal infections and belongs to the echinocandin class of drugs. It is administered intravenously, typically once daily over 1 hour. Dosage and treatment duration depend on the patient's medical condition, response to treatment, and concurrent medications. Pediatric dosages are based on body size. If used at home, patients should learn preparation and usage instructions from healthcare professionals. Before use, inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Infusion reactions may occur during administration. Continue the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms resolve early. Common side effects include injection site swelling/redness/irritation, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, and headache. Serious allergic reactions are rare. This is not a complete list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using caspofungin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other echinocandin antifungal drugs (e.g., anidulafungin, micafungin), or any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone overdoses and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., liver/kidney function, potassium blood levels) should be performed while using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If a dose is missed, consult your doctor or pharmacist for a new dosing schedule. Consult product instructions and your pharmacist for storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
